models._description: Partner Tags - These tags can be used on website to find customers by sector, or ...

behavioral_notes.observation: The /customers listing is a sudo() public directory of published customer references. The base domain is [('website_published','=',True),('assigned_partner_id','!=',False)] -- a partner only appears if it is published AND has an assigned reseller/partner (assigned_partner_id from website_crm_partner_assign), so a 'customer reference' = a published res.partner attached to a partner-program assignment. Optional facets stack onto the domain: free-text search OR-matches name / website_description / industry_id.name; tag_id (unslugged) filters on website_tag_ids; industry and country path segments add equality filters. The controller runs two _read_group calls (by industry_id, by country_id) over the same domain to build the faceted sidebar counts before search_count + paginated search. All queries are sudo() so anonymous visitors can read otherwise-restricted partner data.

website_customer subclasses GoogleMap (from website_google_map) and overrides _get_gmap_domains: when dom == 'website_customer.customers' it returns [('assigned_partner_id','!=',False)] plus current_country / current_industry equality filters. This feeds the JSON map endpoint the front-end Google Maps widget calls to plot reference partners as geolocated markers; the page passes request.website.google_maps_api_key into the template so the map renders client-side. Geolocation/marker data is produced by this domain hook, not by any field on res.partner.tag -- invisible to metadata.

Paging uses request.website.pager(step=_references_per_page=20, scope=7) with url_args=post so search/tag query-string state survives navigation; the pager URL is rebuilt as /customers[/industry/<id>][/country/<id>]. Country handling has a graceful fallback: if a requested country has zero matching references but other countries do, fallback_all_countries is set, country is reset to None, and the full set is shown instead of a 404. Industry counts inject an 'All Industries' aggregate row, and a selected-but-empty industry is appended with count 0 so the active facet still renders. None of this faceting/fallback logic is derivable from the schema.

behavioral_notes.element: res.partner.tag + website.published.mixin (how a partner becomes a public reference)
behavioral_notes.observation: Publishing is governed by website.published.mixin (website/models/mixins.py): it adds website_published (related to is_published, index=True), a computed website_url, and the website_publish_button() toggle. res.partner.tag _inherits the mixin and overrides _default_is_published()=True, so tags are public by default; the listing only shows tags where website_published=True AND partner_ids intersect the current page's partners (ordered by classname, name). The partner itself carries website_published via the same mixin chain pulled in through website_partner / website_crm_partner_assign, and website_description (sanitized Html from website_partner) supplies the reference body. Thus a public reference is materialised by flipping website_published on a res.partner that already has an assigned_partner_id -- a cross-module publishing convention, not a single field.

The UX is server-rendered QWeb (website_customer.index / .details, ~590 XML LOC) calling website.layout, with Bootstrap offcanvas faceted filters (industry/country/tag), a GET search form, and a responsive pager. Client-side JS is minimal (2 JS files, 1 XML template, asset bundle website.website_builder_assets): the only interactive component is the Google Maps reference map fed by the GoogleMap JSON endpoint. No OWL components, registry adds, or patches -- a classic published-content page, not a builder surface.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_customer is a value-network feature of the website storefront (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating technology): it publishes the company's customer base as a curated social-proof directory that mediates between prospective buyers and the population of existing customers/references, with worth that grows as more references, industries and countries are published (directory network effect). It is not a sequential transformation (chain) nor a problem-solving cycle (shop). activity_class is primary because the module's whole purpose is the public-facing marketing artefact -- the 'Our References' page is a demand-side marketing/sell asset, not a back-office support function. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services fits because publishing customer references is a marketing / social-proof activity that supports demand generation and selling; the page exists to market the company through its customers, aligning with the parent website module's 3.0 web-presence classification rather than 6.0 customer service.
